title: Iteratively computing ways to climb stairs from initial states
summary: Starting from the initial states dp[1] = 1 and dp[2] = 2, repeatedly sum the two preceding entries from left to right up to dp[9].
context: Each move climbs 1 or 2 steps, and dp[i] denotes the number of ways to reach step i. This figure shows bottom-up dynamic programming filling the table iteratively without a recursion call stack.
description: First set dp[1] = 1 and dp[2] = 2, then compute dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2] in order from dp[3] through dp[9]: each entry depends only on the preceding two entries, both of which have already been computed when needed.

Nine cells are arranged horizontally in the figure, labeled only with the state names dp[1] through dp[9], while the initial values dp[1] = 1, dp[2] = 2 and the state transition equation are written below. The values 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34, and finally 55 at dp[9] are derived from those initial values and the equation rather than printed inside the cells. The table below lists each state's initial value or dependency together with its derived value.

frames.title: Iteratively computing ways to climb stairs from initial states
frames.explanation: Bottom-up iteration computes each state only once and stops upon reaching the target state; from the initial values and transition equation in the figure, the target state dp[9] evaluates to 55 ways.
